title: Universal property of the integral saturated chart construction
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, $S$ a finitely generated commutative monoid, written additively, and $\beta:S\to(A,\cdot)$ a monoid homomorphism. Use group completion as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], put $S^{\rm int}=\operatorname{im}(S\to S^{\rm gp})$, and put
$$S^{\rm fs}=\{u\in S^{\rm gp}:\exists n>0,\ nu\in S^{\rm int}\}.$$
Suppose $S^{\rm fs}$ is finitely generated. For a commutative monoid $T$, $\mathbf Z[T]$ is the ring of finite sums of monomials $z^t$, with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. Set $B=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S]}\mathbf Z[S^{\rm fs}]$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], where $z^s\mapsto\beta(s)$, and suppose $B$ is Noetherian. Give $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the associated log structure of the chart $S^{\rm fs}\to B$, $u\mapsto1\otimes z^u$, as in [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. Then $C$ is an fs log scheme. For every locally Noetherian fs log scheme $(T,M_T)$, composition with $C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the chart $S\to M_C$ gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\log}(T,C)\simeq\{(v,\lambda):v:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A\text{ a scheme map},\ \lambda:S\to\Gamma(T,M_T)\text{ a monoid map},\ \alpha_T\lambda=v^\sharp\beta\}.$$
Here $v^\sharp$ is the induced map on global regular functions; the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in the right hand side carries no specified log structure. Naturality is with respect to fs log morphisms of $T$ and restriction to open subschemes of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101 (saturation); X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164 ((Pint)sat and the chart of the fs product). This universal-property formulation is agent supplied, not a quotation; WANTED Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, section 1, integralization and saturation.

proof.text: Put $G=S^{\rm gp}$ and $P=S^{\rm fs}$. The image $S^{\rm int}$ generates $G$ as a group. Every element of $G$ is a difference of elements of this image, so the group completions of $S^{\rm int}$ and of the intervening submonoid $P\subset G$ identify with $G$. If $nu$ and $mv$ belong to $S^{\rm int}$, then $nm(u+v)$ belongs to $S^{\rm int}$; thus $P$ is a submonoid. If $ku\in P$ for $k>0$, then $nku\in S^{\rm int}$ for some $n>0$, whence $u\in P$. It follows that $P$ is integral and saturated. Its assumed finite generation makes it fs. All of these checks take place in $G$, allowing torsion.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; agent-supplied universal-property argument, step 1

proof.text: The affine scheme $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is locally Noetherian: the single affine open $C$ has the Noetherian coordinate ring $B$. Apply the associated-log construction to $P\to B$, $u\mapsto1\otimes z^u$. Its geometric stalk is the prescribed pushout of $P$ and local units, so the canonical map from $P$ is a chart in the definition of fs log schemes. Since $P$ is fs by Step 1, this makes $C$ an fs log scheme, including when $B=0$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; agent-supplied universal-property argument, step 2

proof.text: Given a pair $(v,\lambda)$ on the right, put $H=\Gamma(T,M_T)$. The sections lemma makes $H$ integral and saturated. The map $\lambda$ extends by the group-completion relations to $\lambda^{\rm gp}:G\to H^{\rm gp}$. For $u\in P$ choose $n>0$ with $nu$ the image of some $s\in S$. Then $n\lambda^{\rm gp}(u)=j(\lambda(s))$, where $j:H\hookrightarrow H^{\rm gp}$. Saturation gives $\lambda^{\rm gp}(u)\in j(H)$, and injectivity of $j$ defines a unique $\widetilde\lambda(u)\in H$. The equality in the group completion proves additivity and extension of $\lambda$. Uniqueness follows since the induced group homomorphism is already fixed on the generators from $S$; it does not require uniqueness of arbitrary $n$th roots in $H$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; agent-supplied universal-property argument, step 3

proof.text:
Write $D=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $\mu=\alpha_T\widetilde\lambda:P\to(D,\cdot)$. Extend $\mu$ linearly to $\mathbf Z[P]\to D$. The formula
$$r\!\left(a\otimes\sum_u b_uz^u\right)=v^\sharp(a)\sum_u b_u\mu(u)$$
is additive and tensor-balanced because $\mu(s)=v^\sharp\beta(s)$ for $s\in S$. The module tensor universal property therefore gives $r:B\to D$. Products of pure monomials are sent to products by additivity of $\widetilde\lambda$; $1$ goes to $1$, so $r$ is a ring map. Pure tensors generate, proving uniqueness with these values. The affine-spectrum adjunction for the arbitrary scheme $T$ gives a unique scheme map $f:T\to C$ inducing $r$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $v$ because both induce $v^\sharp$ on $A$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; agent-supplied universal-property argument, step 4

proof.text: Step 1 makes $P$ finitely generated and integral, and $\beta_C:P\to\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$, $u\mapsto1\otimes z^u$, is a monoid homomorphism. The logification lemma for finitely generated integral charts gives the log structure $L_C(P,\beta_C)$ whose geometric stalk at $\bar c$ is canonically $P\oplus_{E}\mathcal O_{C,\bar c}^\times$ with $E$ the preimage of the local units; so its canonical map from $P$ is a chart, and the associated-log lemma identifies it, compatibly with $P$, with the log structure $M_C$ of the statement. Step 4 says exactly that $\alpha_T\widetilde\lambda=f^\sharp\beta_C$. For the scheme map $a=f:T\to C$ and $K=M_T$, the bijection of the logification lemma gives a unique homomorphism $f^\flat:f^{-1}M_C\to M_T$ compatible with the structural maps and $f^\sharp$ whose map on $P$ is $\widetilde\lambda$, that is, a unique log morphism $F=(f,f^\flat):T\to C$ above $f$ with chart-section map $\widetilde\lambda$. Its restriction to $S$ is the original $\lambda$, so this construction is a right inverse to the stated map.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101; X proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 6, p.164; agent-supplied universal-property argument, step 5

proof.text: Conversely, let $F:T\to C$ be a log morphism and extract $(v,\lambda)$. Its $P$ chart map must be the extension of $\lambda$ in Step 3, by the uniqueness there. Its underlying ring map sends $a\otimes z^u$ to $v^\sharp(a)\alpha_T\widetilde\lambda(u)$, so Step 4 recovers the underlying scheme map. The bijection of the logification lemma, for this underlying map and this $P$ map, then recovers the log map. This proves the two constructions inverse. Under a log morphism $h:T'\to T$, the pullback of $\widetilde\lambda$ extends the pulled-back $S$ map, so uniqueness in Step 3 identifies it with the new extension; the $P$ map of the composite $Fh$ is this pullback by the definition of composition, so the displayed tensor formula and the uniqueness in the logification lemma identify the resulting morphism with $Fh$. For an open $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, restrict to $v^{-1}(U)$ and to $C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U$: the logification lemma restricts $L_C(P,\beta_C)$ to $L_{C_U}(P,\beta_{C_U})$ on the open $C_U=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U$, chart restrictions and the same formula agree there, and uniqueness identifies the morphisms. This proves both required naturalities.
